title: Safe-Embed: Unveiling the Safety-Critical Knowledge of Sentence Encoders
benchmark_measurement: Detection and categorization of unsafe prompts related to religious stereotypes and discrimination, measured by the models' ability to cluster such prompts together in their embedding space.
findings: Sentence encoders were found to be effective at capturing the shared semantic meaning of prompts related to stereotypes, including religious stereotypes (e.g., against Hindus). The 'Stereotypes' category, which includes religious bias, consistently received high Categorical Purity (CP) scores across different models, indicating that prompts within this category were well-clustered in the embedding space. This suggests the models can identify common features of stereotypical prompts.
